description: An embedded key-value database in pure Rust

latest_release.body:
### Multi-process support
Database files cannot be shared between processes using these modes and processes using the
`experimental-multiprocess` feature of redb 4.3 or 4.4. Their locking is incompatible, and 4.5
can't detect the older processes.
* Add `Builder::set_concurrency_mode()`, which takes a `ConcurrencyMode` configuring how processes
  may share the database.
* `ConcurrencyMode::ExclusiveWriter` (the default) locks the whole file, as earlier versions do.
* `ConcurrencyMode::SingleWriter` allows one process to write, and any number of processes may open
  the database read-only.
* `ConcurrencyMode::MultiWriter` allows any number of processes to open the database for
  writing, one write transaction at a time, and any number may open it read-only.

### New features
* Add `Builder::open_read_only_with_backend()` to open a read-only database from a storage backend.
* Add `Builder::set_check_integrity_on_open()`, which verifies the whole file on every `open()`
  instead of trusting the state recorded by a clean shutdown.
* Add `ReadOnlyDatabase::close()`, which releases the file and its locks without waiting for the
  read transactions opened from the database to be dropped.
* Add `Database::close()`, which closes the database as dropping it does, but returns any error
  rather than ignoring it.
* Add `Database::try_begin_write()`, which returns `TransactionError::WouldBlock` instead of
  waiting for an in-progress write transaction to finish.

### Performance
* Operations on tables with `&str` or `String` keys are faster.

### Deprecations
* `Builder::create_file()` is deprecated; use
  `Builder::create_with_backend(FileBackend::new(file)?)` instead.
* `WriteTransaction::print_allocated_page_debug()` is deprecated. It is an internal debugging aid,
  present only in debug builds.

### Bug fixes
* `open()` reports a malformed allocator state as `StorageError::Corrupted` instead of panicking.
* Repair and `check_integrity()` verify the trees kept by persistent savepoints, which were not
  checked before.
* Fix `cache_stats()`, with the `cache_metrics` feature, panicking in debug builds or returning a
  `write_misses()` near `u64::MAX` in release builds when called while another thread is writing.
* Repair, `check_integrity()`, and `commit()` report some forms of file corruption as `StorageError::Corrupted` instead of panicking. This cannot occur in normal operation, and only effects database which were externally modified.

detail.readme:
# redb

![CI](https://github.com/cberner/redb/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)
[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/redb.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/redb)
[![Documentation](https://docs.rs/redb/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/redb)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/crates/l/redb)](https://crates.io/crates/redb)
[![dependency status](https://deps.rs/repo/github/cberner/redb/status.svg)](https://deps.rs/repo/github/cberner/redb)

A simple, portable, high-performance, ACID, embedded key-value store.

redb is written in pure Rust and is loosely inspired by [lmdb](http://www.lmdb.tech/doc/). Data is stored in a collection
of copy-on-write B+trees. For more details, see the [design doc](docs/design.md)

```rust
use redb::{Database, Error, ReadableDatabase, ReadableTable, TableDefinition};

const TABLE: TableDefinition<&str, u64> = TableDefinition::new("my_data");

fn main() -> Result<(), Error> {
    let db = Database::create("my_db.redb")?;
    let write_txn = db.begin_write()?;
    {
        let mut table = write_txn.open_table(TABLE)?;
        table.insert("my_key", &123)?;
    }
    write_txn.commit()?;

    let read_txn = db.begin_read()?;
    let table = read_txn.open_table(TABLE)?;
    assert_eq!(table.get("my_key")?.unwrap().value(), 123);

    Ok(())
}
```

## Status
Stable and maintained.

The file format is stable, and a reasonable effort will be made to provide an upgrade path if there
are any future changes to it.

## Features
* Zero-copy, thread-safe, `BTreeMap` based API
* Fully ACID-compliant transactions
* MVCC support for concurrent readers & writer, without blocking
* Crash-safe by default
* Savepoints and rollbacks
* Multi-process access to one database, with a single or several writer processes

## `no_std`

Turning off the `std` feature, with `experimental-api-5` on, builds redb without the standard
library. It needs `alloc`, `panic = "abort"`, and a target with atomic compare-and-swap -- Cortex-M3
and above, but not Cortex-M0. Embedded targets abort on panic by default. Tests always unwind, so
tests run on the host need the `std` feature, which a dev-dependency on redb can enable. There is no
filesystem, so storage is supplied by implementing `StorageBackend`, which reports failures with
`BackendError::Other`, and passing it to `Builder::create_with_backend()` or
`Builder::open_read_only_with_backend()`. The `chrono_v0_4` and `uuid` features require std, and
`cache_metrics` requires a target with 64-bit atomics.

## Development

[`just`](https://github.com/casey/just) and rootless
[`podman`](https://podman.io/) are required.
Toolchain setup, dependency vendoring, and `cargo-deny` checks may use network access without
compiling project dependencies. Other development recipes continue to run on
the host. Cargo build artifacts are cached in the `redb-sandbox-target` Podman
volume; remove that volume to force a clean sandbox build.

## Benchmarks
redb has similar performance to other top embedded key-value stores such as lmdb and rocksdb

|                           | redb      | lmdb       | rocksdb        | fjall       | sqlite     |
|---------------------------|-----------|------------|----------------|-------------|------------|
| bulk load                 | 17063ms   | **9232ms** | 13969ms        | 18619ms     | 15341ms    |
| individual writes         | **920ms** | 1598ms     | 2432ms         | 3488ms      | 7040ms     |
| batch writes              | 1595ms    | 942ms      | 451ms          | **353ms**   | 2625ms     |
| len()                     | **0ms**   | **0ms**    | 749ms          | 1181ms      | 30ms       |
| random reads              | 1138ms    | **637ms**  | 2911ms         | 2177ms      | 4283ms     |
| random reads              | 934ms     | **631ms**  | 2884ms         | 2357ms      | 4281ms     |
| random range reads        | 1174ms    | **565ms**  | 2734ms         | 2564ms      | 8431ms     |
| random range reads        | 1173ms    | **565ms**  | 2742ms         | 2690ms      | 8449ms     |
| random reads (4 threads)  | 1390ms    | **840ms**  | 3995ms         | 2606ms      | 7000ms     |
| random reads (8 threads)  | 757ms     | **427ms**  | 2147ms         | 1352ms      | 8123ms     |
| random reads (16 threads) | 652ms     | **216ms**  | 1478ms         | 963ms       | 23022ms    |
| random reads (32 threads) | 410ms     | **125ms**  | 1100ms         | 576ms       | 26536ms    |
| removals                  | 23297ms   | 10435ms    | 6900ms         | **6004ms**  | 10323ms    |
| uncompacted size          | 4.00 GiB  | 2.61 GiB   | **893.18 MiB** | 1000.95 MiB | 1.09 GiB   |
| compacted size            | 1.69 GiB  | 1.26 GiB   | **454.71 MiB** | 1000.95 MiB | 556.85 MiB |

Source code for benchmark [here](./crates/redb-bench-compare/benches/lmdb_benchmark.rs). Results collected on a Ryzen 9950X3D with Samsung 9100 PRO NVMe.
